clue.text: Big wave producing damage in front of ship

indicators.note: in tells us the word for damage sits inside the word for the front of a ship

parts.note: the bow is the forward end of a vessel
ill means harm, as in 'meant no ill'

explanation.surface: A huge sea swell wrecks the forward end of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a large rolling sea swell, a big wave.

clue.text: Carry a gun with sleeves rolled up, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: with sleeves rolled up your forearms are uncovered, bare arms

explanation.surface: Someone rolls up their sleeves before taking up a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The constitutional phrase for carrying weapons sounds exactly like 'bare arms', which is how you are with sleeves rolled up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear arms is the idiom for carrying weapons, as in the American Second Amendment.

clue.text: Without vigour of late?

definitions.meaning: lacking energy or spirit, dull and flat
'the late' means the dead, so something of the late is dead, with no spark of being in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of late' looks like 'recently', but read 'the late' as 'the deceased'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless means dull and listless, and also literally dead, like the departed.

clue.text: Neglect to ring a man up

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the name is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: Tim is any man's name, here just a man

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to telephone a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but gives the letter O; 'up' turns TIM into MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect to do something is to leave it out or fail to do it.

clue.text: Swirling mist hides the way forward

indicators.note: hides says one piece is covered over by the other, held inside it
swirling mist is churned about, so its letters are mixed up

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Fog swirls over a road ahead, concealing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is the adjective meaning bold or presumptuous, not a direction of travel; the surface makes it look like the road ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of presumptuous or brash is the same as being bold and unabashed.

clue.text: Not much gain, we hear, for Joel

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: a small gain is a minor profit

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a small return on an investment by a man named Joel.
explanation.walkthrough: Joel is one of the twelve shorter prophetic books of the Old Testament, so a minor prophet; the name looks like an ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel is one of the twelve Minor Prophets of the Hebrew Bible, an example of the category.

clue.text: In the past, one without a hundred

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for one wraps round the other letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Once upon a time, a person lacked a century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' usually means lacking, but here it is the old sense 'outside', so ONE goes round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Revised point I'd raised with Edward

parts.note: E (east) is a point of the compass

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: I'd without the apostrophe gives these letters
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: An editor amended a remark of theirs together with a colleague called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, E; 'raised' turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A revised text has been corrected and amended, as an editor does.

clue.text: Holding up catch on Yorkshire river

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A fish is held up after being caught on a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' reverses NET into TEN. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the holding of an office or property, or the term of that possession.

clue.text: Matter giving rise to scandalous gossip?

definitions.meaning: a matter is a business or concern, as in 'that's my own business'
an illicit romantic liaison is the kind of thing that sets tongues wagging

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a general concern or business and a secret romantic liaison that causes scandal.

clue.text: Idleness indeed

definitions.meaning: split as 'in deed', meaning engaged in a deed, busy acting

explanation.walkthrough: Split 'indeed' into 'in deed': being in a deed is being in action, which as one word means its opposite, idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of doing nothing, the absence of any activity.

clue.text: Their function is to keep all sides in touch

definitions.text: Their function is to keep all sides in touch

parts.words: Their function is to keep all sides in touch
parts.note: reads like a description of diplomats or mediators keeping parties talking, but literally describes building blocks set where two walls meet

explanation.walkthrough: Sounds like negotiators linking factions; really it is the stone placed at a building's angle, binding two walls together.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stones laid at the angle of a building where two walls meet, joining them.

clue.text: Boring makers of laws

indicators.note: of in the sense of 'made of' says the tools are formed from these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The people who make the laws are dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but these tools bore holes; 'of' says they are made from the letters of LAWS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pointed tools that pierce holes in leather or wood, so they make bores.

clue.text: Sounds tired of regular meals

indicators.note: sounds says we take the word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: tired of something is bored with it

explanation.surface: Someone seems weary of eating the same food every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired of' reads as one phrase; split it: 'tired' gives the sound, and 'of' links to the definition. 'Board' means meals provided, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Board means the daily food provided to a lodger, as in full board.

clue.text: Easy to reach but hard to touch

definitions.meaning: close at hand, not far away
tight-fisted, hard to touch for a loan, a dated British sense of stingy

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the dated British use meaning mean with money, hard to 'touch' for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means close by, and in old British usage also stingy or miserly.

clue.text: Quoted as being seen when heard

indicators.note: when heard says the word counts by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: being seen is being spotted, sighted

explanation.surface: Someone's words are repeated as proof that they were spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cited is to be quoted or referred to as an authority.

clue.text: It's not still being eaten, is it?

definitions.text: It's not still being eaten, is it?

parts.words: It's not still being eaten, is it?
parts.note: sounds like asking whether something has been finished off, but 'not still' means wobbling: a quivering dessert

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'yet', but means motionless: the wobbly pudding never keeps still while eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A wobbly set dessert made with gelatine, which quivers rather than staying motionless.

clue.text: Aim to sign evangelists

parts.note: a mission is an aim or purpose
Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Preachers set out to recruit new followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a zodiac sign, not signing up.
explanation.definitionFit: People sent abroad to spread the Christian gospel are evangelists by role.

clue.text: Being solvent, her career is taking off

definitions.meaning: a chemical solvent used to remove paint or varnish
a performer whose job is removing her clothes on stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Solvent' looks like having money, but it is a chemical solvent; 'taking off' looks like success but means undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a paint-removing chemical and a performer who undresses for an audience.

clue.text: Stumbling upon clue for disconnect"

indicators.note: stumbling means tripping clumsily, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver chances on a hint for a word meaning cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumbling upon' looks like 'finding by chance', but 'Stumbling' shuffles UPON and CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to detach things linked together, such as railway carriages.

clue.text: Bishop Latimer on top form

indicators.note: form as a verb means to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new word

explanation.surface: The bishop Latimer is at his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top form' reads as 'at his best', but 'form' remakes LATIMER ON TOP. Hugh Latimer was a real English bishop, which helps the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop who heads a church province is called by this title, so it is a kind of bishop.

clue.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

definitions.text: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?

parts.words: In which the early bird lies awaiting the worm?
parts.note: the proverbial early bird waiting for its prey: a hidden lying-in-wait; 'early' also suggests the morning, AM, and a bird lies in a bush

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the early bird catches the worm; lying hidden awaiting prey is a surprise attack. Read as AM (early) plus BUSH, where a bird might lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise attack from a hidden position is lying in wait for a victim, as a bird waits for a worm.

clue.text: Pulse in fast time, over one fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the previous part sits above the next

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone's heartbeat rises rapidly past 150.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but is an edible seed; 'fast' is fasting, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is a pulse, the edible seed of a leguminous plant.

clue.text: Suitable start for a day's hunting

definitions.meaning: an old word for fitting or proper
the gathering of riders and hounds before a fox hunt sets off

explanation.walkthrough: In British fox hunting the assembly at the start of the day is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fitting in old usage and also the gathering that begins a hunt.

clue.text: Too high a price to be on the level

definitions.text: Too high a price to be on the level

parts.words: Too high a price to be on the level
parts.note: describes a price so excessive it can't be honest, and a slope too sharp to be flat ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the level' means honest, but also flat: the word describes both an exorbitant charge and a sharp incline.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive in cost, and also sharply sloping rather than flat.

clue.text: Duck behind cover on the beach

indicators.note: behind means the first piece is placed after the second

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck takes shelter under a covering by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird or dodging, but is a cricket score of nought, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air bathing place or beach resort.

clue.text: A curious flower

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' meaning strange is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant, the arum lily, with a striking flower-like spathe.

clue.text: He is used to having high scores

definitions.text: He is used to having high scores

parts.words: He is used to having high scores
parts.note: reads like a sportsman or gamer who regularly scores well, but means a singer given high parts in musical scores

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like points in a game; it is printed music.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice singing high parts above the tenor, given the upper lines in a score.

clue.text: Giving speech, don't start mumbling

indicators.note: don't start tells us to drop the opening letter of the word

parts.note: muttering is mumbling indistinctly

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop mumbling while addressing an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the first letter M from MUTTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttering is voicing words, saying them out.

clue.text: Backward students in blunder

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for students from end to beginning

parts.note: pupils are students at school

explanation.surface: Slow learners are making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward students' looks like slow learners, but 'Backward' reverses PUPILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a small mistake, an error or blunder.

clue.text: With respect, this shows how standard has fallen

definitions.text: With respect, this shows how standard has fallen

parts.words: With respect, this shows how standard has fallen
parts.note: reads like a polite complaint about declining quality, but a standard is a flag lowered partway as a mark of respect for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like quality, but it is a flag lowered partway down the pole in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag flown partway down its pole as a sign of mourning shows it lowered respectfully.

clue.text: Score confused with a gross

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the words score and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled score adds up to 144.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like the number 144 next to 'score', but means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse and gross both mean crude or vulgar.
